body:
Two design changes from the maintainer after 3.2.1.

## 1. Buttons, not clickable text, in list and account settings — both clients

Rule: on the List properties screen and the Account screen (and the web's list properties and
settings pages), every action is a real button. Text-style buttons remain only inside dialogs
(Material's confirm/dismiss convention). Concretely on Android (ui/listprops/ListPropsScreen.kt,
ui/accounts/AccountScreen.kt): the name "Save", "Save order", "Save notes", "Duplicate", "Invite",
the pending invite's "Revoke", the close-vote button, the Account screen's currency and initials
"Save" and each session's "Revoke" become `Button`s in the normal (primary) colour, the way "Leave
list" is a button but in the danger colour; the inline category editor's Save/Cancel become small
buttons too (Save filled, Cancel outlined). Sizing: full-width where the form's field is full
width (Save name, Save notes, Save order, Duplicate, Invite), compact in a row otherwise (Revoke
next to a session or invite). On the web (web/src/pages/ListPropsPage.tsx, SettingsPage.tsx and
any other page with the same actions): the same actions use `btn` (primary) — today several use
`btn-icon`, which renders as text; `btn-icon` stays only for real icon buttons (arrows, the pencil).
Check the two clients side by side: same actions, same wording, same colour role.

## 2. The local area reorders like any account

Today the local area is pinned last: `overviewOrder` (ui/AccountOrder.kt) puts non-server accounts
last, `AccountsViewModel.move` refuses to move past it, the drag guard (`canMoveTo`) stops at it,
`AccountRegistry.addLocal` appends it, and the Accounts row has no drag handle. The maintainer
wants it reorderable like the others: order everywhere is the user's `sortOrder` alone (overview
sections, Accounts screen, the Copy-to picker after the list's own account, the new-list picker's
fallback). Give the local row the same drag handle and accessibility actions. Keep the tests that
say "local last" only where they now say "in the user's order". README sentences that say the local
area is last are corrected.
title: List and account settings use buttons, not clickable text (both clients); the local area reorders like any account
